question: Compare the roles of the training, validation and test sets.
answer: The validation set is used for tuning hyperparameters and the test set is used for the final unbiased estimate [S8]. Data leakage occurs when information from outside the training data influences the features, leading to unrealistically good scores [S8].

citations.text: 5. Data Splitting and Cross-Validation Data is usually divided into a training set for fitting, a validation set for tuning hyperparameters and a test set used once for the final unbiased estimate. Using the test set repeatedly for decisions leaks information and makes the estimate optimistic. Data leakage more generally means that information from outside the training data, such as future values or the target itself, influences the features; it produces unrealistically good scores that collapse in production. k-fold cross-validation splits the training data into k equal folds. The model is trained k times, each time holding out a different fold for validation, and the k scores are averaged. Typical values are k = 5 or k = 10. Stratified k-fold preserves the class proportions in every fold and is recommended for classification with imbalanced classes.

S1.title: Ml Reference Notes
S1.text: training and validation data because the model is too simple. Bias: error from wrong or overly simple assumptions.  Variance: error from sensitivity to the specific training sample. Cross-validation: repeated training on different train/validation splits to estimate performance reliably. Data leakage: using information during training that would not be available at prediction time. Confusion matrix: a table of TP, FP, TN and FN counts. Precision: TP / (TP + FP). Recall: TP / (TP + FN). F1: harmonic mean of precision and recall. ROC AUC: area under the receiver operating characteristic curve; 0.5 means random ranking. Imbalanced data: classes occur with very different frequencies. One-hot encoding: representing a category as a binary vector with a single 1. Standardization: rescaling to mean 0 and standard deviation 1.

S2.title: Ml Exercise Guide
S2.text:
Assignment 1: Diagnosing a Model
Task. You trained a decision tree classifier and obtained 99% training accuracy but 71% validation accuracy. Explain what is happening and propose two fixes.
Expected answer. The large gap between training and validation accuracy is the signature of overfitting (high variance). Fixes include limiting the maximum depth of the tree, requiring a minimum number of samples per leaf, pruning, switching to a random forest, or collecting more data. Report validation performance using cross-validation rather than a single split.

S3.title: Ml Reference Notes
S3.text: Feature: an input variable used by a model, for example a person's age. Label or target: the value the model should predict. Hyperparameter: a setting chosen before training, such as the learning rate, tree depth or number of neighbors k. Parameter: a value learned during training, such as the weights of linear regression. Epoch: one full pass through the training data. Batch size: the number of examples used for one gradient update. Learning rate: the step size of gradient descent. Regularization: a penalty that discourages overly complex models. L2 (ridge) shrinks weights; L1 (lasso) can set weights to zero. Overfitting: low training error but high validation error because the model memorized noise. Underfitting: high error on both training and validation data because the model is too simple. Bias: error from wrong or overly simple assumptions.

S4.title: Ml Model Diagnostics Handbook
S4.text:
1. Reading Learning Curves
A learning curve plots training error and validation error against the training set size. In a high-bias
model both errors are high and they converge close to each other; adding more data barely helps
because the model is too simple. In a high-variance model the training error is low and a large gap
separates it from the validation error; the validation error keeps falling as more data is added, so
collecting more data helps.
When a model is overfitting the first actions to try are a simpler model, stronger regularization,
more training data or early stopping.

S5.title: Ml Lecture Notes
S5.text: 3. Generalization, Overfitting and the Bias-Variance Tradeoff A model generalizes when it performs well on new data, not just on the data used for training. Overfitting happens when a model memorizes noise and idiosyncrasies of the training set: training error is very low but validation or test error is much higher. Underfitting happens when the model is too simple to capture the pattern, so both training and validation error are high. The bias-variance tradeoff explains this. Bias is the error caused by overly simple assumptions; high-bias models underfit. Variance is the sensitivity of a model to the particular training sample; high-variance models overfit. Total expected error is bias squared plus variance plus irreducible noise. Increasing model complexity lowers bias but raises variance.

S6.title: Ml Exercise Guide
S6.text:
Assignment 3: Preventing Data Leakage
Task. A student standardizes the whole dataset, then splits it into train and test sets. What is wrong?
Expected answer. The scaler computed the mean and standard deviation using the test rows, so information from the test set leaked into the training pipeline. The correct procedure is to split first, fit the scaler on the training set only and apply the fitted scaler to the test set. Using a scikit-learn Pipeline inside cross-validation automates this.

S7.title: Ml Evaluation Protocol V1
S7.text:
Split the data 60% training, 20% validation and 20% test.
Use k = 10 folds for cross-validation.
The primary metric is accuracy.
Fix the random seed to 0.

S9.title: Ml Project Handbook
S9.text:
Evaluation Protocol v2
Evaluation protocol v2 supersedes protocol v1 for all projects started in 2025. Split the data 70% training, 15% validation and 15% test. Use k = 5 folds for cross-validation and report the mean and standard deviation of the fold scores. Set random_state=42 everywhere. The test set may be used exactly once. The primary metric is F1 for imbalanced data and accuracy otherwise.
